The ocean does not care about your metaphors. It does not know it resembles eternity or grief or the unconscious mind. It simply moves, obeying the ancient choreography of moon and wind, folding and unfolding like a cloth that can never be fully spread. She sat on the rocks and watched it, her notebook open, her pen still. She had come here to write, but the ocean had made writing seem both urgent and absurd... urgent because it was so overwhelmingly present, absurd because no sentence could hold it. The waves broke against the stones with a sound like applause, or perhaps like the opposite of applause... like the world slowly taking something back. Seabirds carved arcs above the spray, white against grey, calligraphy of instinct. She wrote one line: the sea is not a metaphor. Then she crossed it out, because even that was a kind of metaphoring. She closed the notebook. She listened. The ocean continued its indifferent psalm, older than language, patient as stone, beautiful beyond the reach of every word she knew.
